title: Using a Model as a Judge
summary: When answers are open-ended and no single reference exists, a second model can grade them against a rubric. This lesson shows how to set that up, how to measure whether the judge agrees with people, and how to detect and correct its biases.
objectives: Design a pointwise or pairwise judge prompt with a clear rubric and choose between the two
Compute agreement rate and Cohen's kappa between a judge and human labels
Measure position bias with order swapping and verbosity bias with length-stratified comparisons
Compute win rates with ties and relate them to Bradley-Terry strength differences
Correct a judge-estimated pass rate using the judge's true and false positive rates
prerequisites: Precision, recall and thresholds from [Success Criteria](/learn/evaluation/success-criteria), and the reference metrics from [Scoring Against References](/learn/evaluation/reference-scoring), whose failures motivate judges.
